sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of all leave requests for a given employee; status: filtering by status (SUBMITTED for manager approval queues, APPROVED for calendar views); start_date, end_date: range queries for calendar views and overlapping-leave detection; employee_id, status: combined filter for 'my pending requests' queries; approved_by: manager approval queue lookups

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, fiscal_year, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id, leave_type, fiscal_year: unique-lookup for a specific employee's balance for a given leave type and year — the dominant access pattern when checking available days before applying; employee_id: all-balances-for-employee queries (dashboard views)

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, fiscal_year, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id, leave_type, fiscal_year: dominant access pattern — checking available balance before applying for leave; must be unique to prevent duplicate balance rows; employee_id: dashboard queries fetching all balances for an employee

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type, is_active: dominant lookup — find the active policy for a given leave type when validating a request; is_active: filtering active policies in admin views

table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup for auth and notifications; manager_id: team-listing queries for manager dashboards; employment_status: filtering active employees for leave eligibility

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit-trail lookups for a specific entity (e.g. all changes to leave_request #123); performed_by: audit queries by actor; performed_at: time-range audit queries

data_notes:
Tables defined: leave_requests (core leave application entity with status lifecycle), leave_balances (per-employee/per-type/per-year entitlement tracking), leave_policies (policy configuration for each leave type), employees (referenced by leave_requests and leave_balances; defined here because the leave module depends on it), audit_logs (GP-002 compliance for all state-changing operations). 

The leave_balances table uses (employee_id, leave_type, fiscal_year) as a logical unique key — the repository's upsert method enforces this. The leave_requests table stores leave_type as a string enum value (annual, sick, emergency) rather than a foreign key to leave_policies, because the policy may change over time but the request must retain the type at time of application.

Repositories: PgLeaveRequestRepository, PgLeaveBalanceRepository, PgLeavePolicyRepository, PgEmployeeRepository, PgAuditLogRepository — all backed by the shared pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts.

Open question: day-counting semantics (inclusive/exclusive, weekends) — recorded as BR-001-style openQuestion to avoid silent inconsistency across balance updates.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted — are start_date and end_date inclusive, and do weekends/public holidays count toward the used-days total?
open_questions.impact: Affects the used_days calculation in leave_balances when a request is approved. If weekends are excluded, the day-counting logic must integrate a calendar or weekday-computation function. The choice propagates to every balance update and to the overlapping-leave detection query.
candidate_options: Calendar days inclusive (start_date through end_date, all days count)
Business days only (exclude weekends; holidays handled separately)
Calendar days but end_date is exclusive (end_date - start_date)

transaction_contract: Multi-step writes that must be atomic: (1) approving a leave request updates leave_requests.status + leave_balances.used_days/remaining_days; (2) cancelling an already-approved request reverts the status + restores balance days. Repository methods that must join a caller's transaction (updateStatus on ILeaveRequestRepository, updateUsedDays on ILeaveBalanceRepository) accept an optional pg PoolClient parameter. When omitted, each method uses the shared pool and runs in its own implicit transaction. The calling service (LeaveService) owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, executes BEGIN, passes the client to each repository method, then COMMIT or ROLLBACK.
